items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: I never argued with them because I've never known them to do anything dishonest.

ctx.x: I sure lots of guys didn't pay. But most of the guys did.

Well, you know, sometimes I would forget to pay and they would say, you know, you owe $50, $60.00. I would never question them. I'd say, I'm sorry, here, you know. I never argued with them because I've never known them to do anything dishonest.

I can remember going to Europe, right after Ben left in 1960, in the '60s, Ben Webster left to go to Europe, and he left right from this place where we used to stay, right here where we're doing this tape, this is the last place he lived in the United States. Ben slept right there and we used to have some jam sessions down here. And his passport, after he died, had this as his resident address on it.
